rows.evidence: src/executor.jl:578 gives every PhaseBody with no gated entry, `rhs` included, a one-argument method that walks the interior. test/test_executor.jl:139-143 calls `rhs(3)` and asserts it writes what `rhs()` writes. test/test_executor.jl:2-3 and :15 describe the roster as total in both arities, and :17-22 assert `@ballocated($body(1)) == 0` for `rhs` too.
rows.fix: `rhs` gates on no index. Its one-argument form walks the same continuous entries, so the roster stays total in both arities.
rows.note: The loop itself calls `rhs()` alone (src/model.jl:621, :634). The difference is in the accessor's surface, not in the loop.

rows.claim: At -O0 the trajectories differ from -O2's by round-off, so a trace recorded at one level does not replay bit for bit at the other.
rows.evidence: probe:92 prints feedback_model's xbuf after run! to t=1. It is [0.43970864059724774, 0.18270426549422475] at both -O2 and -O0, bit for bit.
rows.note: One small linear fixture agrees bit for bit, which does not refute a general caution. Settling it needs a model whose arithmetic the optimizer reassociates or contracts, such as a muladd or SIMD reduction, or the measurement in design/reports/20261001_compile_cost_reeval/.

rows.claim: The snapshot's reference fields (field handles) add no per-boundary allocation either way.
rows.evidence: src/store.jl:149 `capture_stores` copies every eltype block, and a handle type is its own eltype block (test/test_store.jl:263-264). So a handle adds one buffer copy per published boundary. probe:79-80 counts 8 allocations per capture on handle_model (two blocks) against 6 on feedback_model (one block). probe:85 confirms the bulk data is shared, not copied.
rows.fix: The reference fields add no garbage beyond their block's one buffer copy per boundary, a copy that shares the bulk data.
rows.note: Borderline. Any extra eltype costs the same one copy, so the verifier may read 'either way' (isbits or not) as satisfied. The two probe models differ, so the count is indicative, but store.jl:149 settles the mechanism.

rows.claim: A scheduled `GC.gc(false)` at frame boundaries moves collection out of the critical path.
rows.evidence: No `GC.` call exists in src/ (rg 'GC\.' src/ finds none). design/pending.md:229-233 records that §9.8 names `GC.gc(false)` at frame boundaries and nothing in `src/` builds it. Lead: `GC.gc` missing at spec.md:6415.
rows.fix: Docs: 'A scheduled `GC.gc(false)` at frame boundaries would move collection out of the critical path. Nothing schedules it yet (pending).' Code: schedule a young collection in the pacer's wait, per design/pending.md:229.
rows.note: pending.md records the gap as open analysis work, not a settled build. The verifier may prefer drift or a recorded deviation over defect. The Bumper.jl sentence beside it is advice, with no framework support claimed, and is counted as why.
